**No paper or document came through with your question.** The working directory is empty, so I can't tell which model you mean. RACE-h results appear in several papers.

My best guess is **GPT-1** (Radford et al., 2018, *"Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training"*). If that's the one, these are the RACE-h figures as I recall them from its Table 3:

- **GPT-1 on RACE-h:** 57.4% accuracy
- **Previous best:** 50.3%, from the BiAttention MRU ensemble (Tay et al., 2018)

That's a gain of about 7 points. For context, the same table reports RACE-m at 62.9 (vs. 60.2) and overall RACE at 59.0 (vs. 53.3).

If you meant a different paper, the numbers will be quite different. XLNet, RoBERTa and ALBERT all report RACE-high scores in the 80s. Please share the paper or its title and I'll check the exact figures rather than relying on memory.
